text:
alex: Heads up — I noticed a prod deploy where ArgoCD started syncing a service before the Terraform changes that create its ConfigMap were applied. App came up with missing envs and 500s. Anyone seen this race before?

lina: Oof. Is this for the new payment-feature branch?

alex: yes, ran via GH Actions -> merge -> argo sync. Atlantis plan/apply was queued but slow because of the workspace lock. ArgoCD pulled the new k8s manifests referencing the new configmap name.

tim: This is the classic ordering problem. We either gate ArgoCD on an infra-ready signal or make k8s manifest tolerant to missing config. Which do we prefer?

sara: Prefer gating infra first for this flow. We should not let Git merge + Argo sync go ahead until atlantis apply finishes.

lina: Agreed. Quick options: 1) make GH Actions require a status check that Atlantis sets after apply; 2) have ArgoCD ignore the commit until repo status is green; 3) add a short retry loop in the app container for missing secrets (not ideal).

alex: For (1) does Atlantis set a status? We use atlantis server that comments, but not a Git status by default.

tim: We can add a tiny GH Action that waits for Atlantis apply via the PR comment or use a repo status set by an action run triggered by Atlantis. Example pattern: Atlantis triggers a small workflow_dispatch (or repo status) on apply completion.

ci-bot: CI: example idea — add a workflow that runs on workflow_dispatch, then sets a commit status via the GitHub Checks API. Could be invoked by Atlantis webhook.

lina: Another pragmatic approach: switch the ArgoCD auto-sync webhook to require the branch to have a check named "infra/applied" present. ArgoCD supports ignoring commits via annotations but not native checks; we'd do it in the webhook receiver.

alex: Can we sketch a small GH Action that listens for an Atlantis success comment and then flips a check? Something like:
```yaml
on: issue_comment
if: contains(github.event.comment.body, '/atlantis apply')
jobs:
  set-check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Set infra/applied check
        run: |
          gh api repos/:owner/:repo/check-runs -f name='infra/applied' -f status='completed' -f conclusion='success' -F head_sha=${{ github.event.issue.pull_request.head.sha }}
```

tim: That could work but we need Atlantis to actually call/comment once apply finishes. Does our Atlantis instance post apply comments? I think we only comment on plan by default.

sara: We can enable the post-apply comment in Atlantis config: set 'post_apply_comment: true' or use the webhook integration to forward apply events to a small service that sets the check. Ops could do a minimal lambda to translate Atlantis webhooks -> GitHub check.

alex: What about short-term mitigation? Could we set ArgoCD to wait on the K8s secret presence by adding an annotation to the app that blocks sync until the configmap exists? I saw a pattern where apps have an initHook that waits for resource.

lina: That helps for future quick patches but still feels like bandaid. Root cause is merge -> argo sync pathway proceeding ahead of infra apply.

ops-bot: OPS: I can add a small validation to our repo merge workflow: if PR modifies infra/* files, require a gate step that waits for 'infra/applied' check. Want me to open a PR?

alex: Yes please. Also we should add a retry/backoff to the app startup as defense in depth.

tim: Action items: (1) ops opens PR to add infra gate in merge job, (2) enable Atlantis post-apply webhook/commenting, (3) small bridge service or action to set 'infra/applied' check on success, (4) app-level short retry for missing envs.

sara: I'll take (2) and (3). Will pair with infra to validate webhook secrets (SQS -> lambda or direct GH check).

lina: I'll do (1) PR for merge workflow changes. Will add logic: if changed files include 'terraform/**' or 'infra/**' then require 'infra/applied' check.

alex: Thanks. If anyone hits the 500 again, ping me and I'll roll the Argo sync back for that PR.

tim: One more note — consider using a dedicated S3-backed atlantis lock workspace per PR so apply doesn't get delayed by unrelated projects. Less lock contention = fewer races.

sara: Good call. Adding that to infra backlog.

alex: Awesome, thanks all. :thumbsup:
